Urban planners study restaurants as anchors in neighborhood networks.

s.defn: Of or relating to restaurants or the restaurant industry; used to describe features, practices, or contexts typical of dining establishments.
ex: The study categorized staffing patterns using a restaurant-related framework.
Researchers compared dining room layouts with restaurant-related design principles.

s.defn: Relating to or denoting styling, equipment, or presentation that imitates or aligns with the typical appearance or operation of restaurants; used to classify products or services designed to mimic restaurant aesthetics or standards.
ex: The lab evaluated restaurant-grade appliances for reliability.
A restaurant-style ambiance was simulated in the classroom setting.

s.defn: an informal interjection used to say goodbye when parting.
ex: Okay, I have to go now, bye.
We finished the call; bye, see you tomorrow.

s.defn: An automatic advance to the next round in a school or club tournament when there is no opponent to play.
ex: The bracket awarded a bye to the team because there were no other players in the bracket.
The school tournament granted a bye to the undefeated team in the first round.

s.defn: An expression used to say goodbye as people part ways.
ex: Students said bye as they left the classroom.
We waved and said bye to our guests.

s.defn: A public road in a city or town, typically lined with buildings and designated for vehicle and pedestrian use.

Urban planners analyze street traffic to optimize mobility on arterial routes.

s.defn: The street as a social and cultural milieu in urban environments, referring to everyday life and public interaction.
ex: Sociologists study street life as a site of informal exchange.
Artists and researchers examine street markets as nodes of urban culture.

s.defn: Relating to streets or the street environment; pertaining to urban streets or the public thoroughfare.
ex: Street oriented data collection examines how pedestrians interact with sidewalks and crossings.
Street infrastructure features influence traffic and safety in urban districts.

s.defn: Having practical knowledge of urban life; street-smart.
ex: The streetwise graduate leveraged local contacts to recruit participants.
A streetwise approach to fieldwork improves participant engagement.

Calling someone a pig signals disapproval of unclean or selfish conduct.

s.defn: Pig as a pejorative term for a police officer referring to law enforcement personnel.

s.defn: A form of structured competitive play governed by rules and designed for recreation or sport.

Students discuss strategies during a cooperative game exercise.

s.defn: Wild animals hunted for sport or for food.

Game species require careful management to prevent overharvest.

s.defn: A formal model of strategic interaction used in game theory describing players, strategies, payoffs, and outcomes.

Nash equilibrium is a concept in game theory.

s.defn: To participate in a game or competitive activity under rules; to engage in play.

s.defn: To manipulate or exploit rules or processes to gain advantage, often unfairly.

s.defn: eager or willing to participate in an activity or challenge; not reluctant.
ex: The team was game to try the new experimental procedure.
The students were game for the field trial.

s.defn: relating to animals hunted for sport or to edible meat obtained from them.
ex: Game meats require careful handling to preserve flavor.
Game birds are a traditional staple in some cuisines.

s.defn: A spoken exchange of ideas between two or more participants that is typically informal and iterative.
ex: Researchers conducted a conversation to compare qualitative methods.
A short conversation revealed cultural norms in workplace communication.

s.defn: A formal discussion among participants typically conducted to reach a decision or exchange professional views.
ex: The committee engaged in a formal conversation to resolve budget questions.
During the conference, a structured conversation addressed policy implications.

s.defn: In linguistics and discourse analysis, the organization of interactive turns and related talk exchange within spoken language.
ex: In discourse analysis, conversation patterns reflect turn taking dynamics.
Backchanneling cues accompany conversation to signal attentiveness.

s.defn: The numeral 1 used to denote a single unit in counting and arithmetic.

We write one to show a single unit in math.

s.defn: A particular person or thing singled out as the one chosen or preferred.
ex: The one selected for demonstration is the team captain.
We chose the one correct answer after checking all steps.

s.defn: the quantity of one; a single unit used to modify a noun
ex: Only one student completed the problem before class.
Place one page of notes on the desk.

s.defn: occurring or used only one time
ex: The experiment was a one-off study requiring careful documentation.
This policy is one-time and will not be repeated.

s.defn: A pronoun used to refer to an unspecified person in a general statement.
ex: One should always check before borrowing.
If one can do it, anyone can.

s.defn: A cardinal numeral determiner used to designate a single item in a countable set, modifying the noun that follows.
ex: I have one dog in my family.
Choose one correct answer from the choices.

s.defn: Used to indicate a single, selected member of a larger group, often appearing in one of constructions.
ex: One of the students raised her hand.
Take one of the apples from the basket.

s.defn: Used in fixed phrases to express exclusivity or emphasis that there is only a single, unique option.
ex: This is the one and only champion.
She is the one option we need.

s.defn: The flat horizontal surface within a room or building on which occupants stand, place objects, or perform activities, typically finished with wood, tile, carpet, or other materials.
ex: The floor was swept clean before the performance.
A marble floor reflected the chandelier's light.

s.defn: A distinct horizontal level within a building used for occupancy or activity, including spaces such as ground floor and upper floors.
ex: The meeting took place on the third floor.
Elevators connect all floors of the building.

s.defn: The greatest integer less than or equal to a real number, a standard mathematical function that maps a real value to an integer.
ex: The floor of 3.7 is 3.
For any real x, floor x is an integer.

s.defn: To cause someone to fall to the floor as a result of a physical strike, push, or other force; to overpower or immobilize by force.
ex: The assailant floored the guard with a swift punch.
The officer was floored when the suspect lunged forward, but recovered quickly.

s.defn: To lay or install a floor surface or to cover a space with a floor material such as wood, tile, or carpet.
ex: Contractors floor the library with oak planks.
We floor the dining hall using reclaimed wood.

s.defn: To apply the floor function to a numeric value, yielding the greatest integer less than or equal to the value.
ex: The calculator floors 3.9 to 3.
We floor a positive decimal to the floor value.

s.defn: To press the accelerator pedal to the floor, maximizing engine power and speed.
ex: The driver floors the accelerator to escape.
During overtaking, floor the accelerator to gain speed.

s.defn: Here denotes a deictic locative adverb indicating the location of an entity relative to the speaker, i.e., in this place.
ex: The sample was collected here for analysis.
The data are here on the table for review.

s.defn: Interjection used to indicate the speakers presence at a location or to designate the location under discussion in scholarly discourse.
ex: Here is the dataset used for the analysis.
Participants stood here during the calibration phase.

s.defn: Used to draw attention to a following statement or example; functions as an attention-getting device in expository writing.
ex: Here we present the main result to illustrate the model.
Here the data indicate a significant correlation between variables.

s.defn: An emphatic interjection used to highlight a notable claim or to mark a transition; often used to emphasize a discovery or a conclusion.
ex: Here lies the central contradiction in the argument.
Here lies an unexamined assumption that requires scrutiny.

s.defn: Bread is a baked edible product produced from dough of flour and water, typically leavened with yeast; consumed as a staple food in many cultures.
ex: Artisanal bread varieties vary in crust and crumb.
White bread production was analyzed under controlled fermentation conditions.

s.defn: Bread is slang for money; money or financial resources used for daily living.
ex: In everyday discourse bread stands for money.
Policy discussions treat bread as a measure of wealth.

s.defn: To coat or crust food with breadcrumbs or a breadcrumb like coating prior to cooking, typically to create a crisp texture and enhanced flavor in culinary preparation.
ex: The chef breaded the cod before frying.
She breaded zucchini slices for the pan.

s.defn: Interrogative determiner used to identify one or more items from a defined set within a question or comparison in academic discourse.
ex: Which method yields the highest accuracy in this experiment?
Which dataset will be used to validate the model's performance?

s.defn: Restrictive relative determiner used to introduce a relative clause that specifies which subset of items is being referred to in an academic statement.
ex: The theory which explains the anomaly remains widely debated.
The datasets which were used in the replication study are deposited.

s.defn: Which functions as an interrogative determiner or interrogative pronoun used to identify a specific item from a defined set.
ex: Which column should I cite in the bibliography?
Which of these theories best explains the phenomenon?

s.defn: Which functions as a relative pronoun introducing a relative clause that refers to a previously mentioned noun or noun phrase, providing additional specification.
ex: The dataset which was collected last year supports the hypothesis.
The author which you referenced argued for a different conclusion.

s.defn: My is a possessive determiner that marks ownership by the first person speaker and precedes a noun to indicate possession.
ex: My results indicate a significant effect on the dependent variable.
My dataset comprises 1,024 observations collected over two years.

s.defn: At all times; on every occasion; without exception.
ex: The dataset remained always complete across all trials.
The protocol is designed to be always applicable in the laboratory setting.

s.defn: Used to indicate that a statement is true in all circumstances; used as an intensifier or discourse marker to denote universality.
ex: Researchers should always report negative results.
The theorem is always assumed to hold under listed conditions.

s.defn: A printed or electronic list of dishes offered by a restaurant, typically organized by course and category, intended for patrons to select meals.
ex: The menu lists soups and salads for today.
Seasonal menus reflect regional produce and chef specialties.

s.defn: A navigational or functional list of commands or options presented by a software interface or device, enabling user selection.
ex: Open the file menu to save changes.
The settings menu groups preferences by category.

s.defn: A set of services, offerings, or products provided by an organization or product as selectable options, often with varying levels or packages.
ex: The hotel offers a menu of services including spa.
The software provides a menu of professional features.

s.defn: Relating to a menu in dining contexts; the list of dishes and items offered by a service.
ex: The menu items were standardized across branches.
The restaurant expanded its seasonal menu.

s.defn: Relating to interfaces that rely on menu navigation for user actions; typically implemented as menu-driven or menu-based interactions.
ex: The software is menu driven.
A menu based interface reduces cognitive load for new users.

s.defn: Relating to the planning and arrangement of meals in dietary contexts or institutional dining; the act of planning meals using a menu.
ex: Menu planning influences nutritional outcomes.
Hospitals implement menu planning to meet dietary guidelines.

s.defn: To study two or more items to note how they are similar and different.
ex: Students compare two textbooks to decide which is clearer.
Researchers compare plants grown in different soils to test effects.

s.defn: To liken or compare as a way to illustrate similarities to something else.
ex: The author compares the hero to a storm to emphasize energy.
Teachers compare the two stories to show shared motifs.

s.defn: To set items against a standard for evaluation; to measure by comparison.
ex: We benchmark student work against the rubric.
The new test is benchmarked with last year's results.

s.defn: A customary unit of length equal to twelve inches used to measure distance.
ex: Measure the desk length and record the result in feet and inches.
A rope that is three feet long equals thirty six inches exactly.

s.defn: The point where a perpendicular meets a line or the base point of a perpendicular in a geometric figure.
ex: Find the foot of the perpendicular from the vertex to the base of the triangle.
Draw the perpendicular and label its foot on the horizontal line accurately.

s.defn: To compute the sum of a column or list of numbers by adding them together, a procedure used when totaling measures or scores.
ex: Foot the column of numbers to find the total length in feet.
Students foot the score column after each round to check totals.

s.defn: To add a measured length expressed in feet into an overall measurement or combined length.
ex: Foot each board measurement so the total project length is correct.
When measuring, foot lengths first then convert to inches if needed.

s.defn: A poor person is an individual who lacks enough money or resources to meet basic needs.
ex: One poor person may need charity for basics.
During the Great Depression, the poor faced shortages.

s.defn: The poor refer to the group of people living in poverty as a social class.
ex: Schools study how the poor benefit from social programs.
The poor often rely on community services for support.

s.defn: Lacking sufficient money or resources not wealthy.
ex: Many families live in poor housing conditions.
Students from poor communities may lack access to resources.

s.defn: Of low quality or standard not meeting expectations.
ex: The report contained poor data due to measurement errors.
Poor design led to unreliable results in the study.

s.defn: Lacking skill or ability in a given area not competent.
ex: The student is a poor reader.
The student is a poor performer in science class.

s.defn: An exclamation used to express sympathy for someone's misfortune in academic or everyday contexts.
ex: Poor you, you forgot your homework before the quiz.
Poor you, your science project was damaged.

s.defn: An interjection expressing sympathy for something or someone in distress, often used with the phrase poor thing to refer to animals or inanimate objects.
ex: Poor thing, the kitten is shivering after the rain.
Poor thing, the old computer is slow but usable.

s.defn: Feeling or showing strong annoyance, displeasure, or hostility, typically in response to perceived provocation, frustration, or interference; often expressed verbally or through facial expression.
ex: The researchers noted an angry response from participants after disclosure of results.
An angry discourse during a debate can undermine collaborative problem solving.

s.defn: Used to describe non-human phenomena or contexts as hostile or threatening, or to indicate a high degree of intensity in a situation, often in figurative usage.
ex: The angry weather disrupted field operations and delayed data collection.
A policy environment characterized by an angry public stance can hinder reform.

s.defn: Widely known or recognized by many people; celebrated for public recognition.
ex: The scientist became famous after winning the prize.
The author is famous for his children's books.

s.defn: Famous for a particular achievement or reason; widely recognized because of a specific contribution.
ex: She is famous for her work in astronomy.
The discovery made him famous in science.

s.defn: A person who is widely known to the public; a celebrity.
ex: The famous often appear at charity events.
The famous from our city visited the museum.

s.defn: A deontic use of should expressing obligation, duty, or normative expectation in academic contexts, weaker than must and indicating what is appropriate or required in a given context.

The protocol should be approved by the ethics board.

s.defn: Expresses advice or a recommendation in analysis or instruction, indicating what is advisable rather than mandatory.

s.defn: Expresses probability or expectation about outcomes given a condition, indicating that an outcome is likely or expected.

s.defn: Used in conditional clauses to introduce a hypothetical or contingent event; indicates contingency rather than assertion.

s.defn: The pronoun used to refer to all things; the totality of items, events, or ideas in a given context.
ex: Everything in the science kit is labeled and stored.
Everything the teacher described relates to the lesson goal.

s.defn: Nineteen, in mathematics and counting, is the natural number that comes after eighteen and before twenty; used as a cardinal number to denote a quantity.

s.defn: The numeral nineteen used attributively to modify a noun to specify a quantity of nineteen.

s.defn: Cardinal numeral used as a determiner before a noun to specify a count of nineteen.

s.defn: To expose a material to sunlight in order to dry or cure it.

s.defn: The act or process of bearing or transporting something from one location to another.

s.defn: Not lit or not functioning; extinguished or unavailable.

s.defn: To express gratitude or appreciation to someone for a specific action, information, or favor, typically in formal or academic contexts.

s.defn: To acknowledge receipt of information or assistance and to express gratitude within formal communications, such as acknowledgments in publications or grant reports.

s.defn: The adjective used to denote the principal physical component or route within a built environment, such as a dominant entrance or thoroughfare.

s.defn: The wife of one’s uncle; a female spouse within the extended family.

s.defn: Sure as an adjective means certain without doubt; something that is sure is highly likely to be true.

s.defn: An interjection used to express agreement or willingness in response to a request or statement.

s.defn: An opening in a wall or vehicle fitted with glass to admit light and provide a view.

s.defn: A well is a deep hole or shaft dug to reach groundwater or other liquids, typically lined to prevent collapse.

ten data points were collected in the study.

the tenth draft received approval after revision.

s.defn: A determiner indicating a large quantity or extent of a noun, typically used with uncountable nouns or with a collective sense; commonly contrasted with many.

s.defn: Great in amount or extent; used before noncount nouns to indicate a large quantity.

s.defn: To participate in cycling as a sport or exercise; to ride a bicycle in a physical activity or sportive context.
ex: Athletes bicycle during training sessions to improve endurance.
Public health studies examine people bicycling for recreation.

s.defn: To make information or ideas clear by describing details or giving examples in a way that someone can understand.
ex: The teacher explains the math rule with a worked example.
In science, students explain how plants make food in their own words.

s.defn: To provide reasons or evidence that support a claim or decision.
ex: The student explains why the answer is correct by listing evidence.
The teacher explains the reasons for the schedule change.

s.defn: To show or describe something by using an example, demonstration, or model to help understanding.
ex: The teacher explains the concept by illustrating with a real experiment.
The student explains the rule by using a diagram.

s.defn: A small, nocturnal mammal of the family Muridae and order Rodentia, typically with a pointed snout, whiskers, rounded ears, and a long tail, widely distributed in natural and human-modified habitats.
ex: Laboratory genetics routinely employ Mus musculus as a model organism.
Field studies document population dynamics of the house mouse.

s.defn: A handheld pointing input device that translates translational motion of the device into cursor movement on a computer interface, typically using optical or ball-based sensors.
ex: The optical mouse relies on LED sensors to track movement.
Ergonomic mice reduce repetitive strain in office workers.

s.defn: A person who is easily frightened or shy; used colloquially to describe someone who avoids risk or exposure.
ex: In social psychology, a timid mouse may avoid novel tasks.
The term timid mouse is used colloquially to describe risk averse individuals.

s.defn: To move and control a computer cursor by operating a mouse, typically to select, open, or interact with on-screen elements.
ex: Participants moused the cursor to highlight the data point in the figure.
Researchers moused over each label to reveal tooltips during the usability test.

s.defn: Not a single thing; the absence of any object or amount.
ex: There is nothing left in the cookie jar.
Nothing will change if we wait.

s.defn: The absence of anything; the state of nonexistence.
ex: There is nothing on the desk after the cleanup.
Students learned that nothing can replace effort in a project.

s.defn: A person or thing of little importance or value.
ex: In the crowd, he appeared as a nobody who spoke rarely.
The character was written as a nonentity in the story.

s.defn: The value of zero in counting, measurement, or scoring.
ex: The score turned to nothing when the last goal was scored, equaling zero.
The balance showed nothing, so the measurement registered as zero.

s.defn: A sentence or phrase used to ask for information.
ex: What is the capital of France and why is it important?
Explain why the plant dies after being overexposed to sunlight.

s.defn: A prompt on a test or assignment that asks for a response.
ex: Which equation solves for x and shows all steps?
List two reasons supporting your argument.

s.defn: A topic or matter to be discussed or considered.
ex: The question of climate change will be discussed in science class.
Today’s big question is how plants make food.

s.defn: To ask questions or seek information from someone in order to gain understanding or clarification; to pose questions as part of learning or inquiry.
ex: In science class, students question the procedure to ensure accuracy.
The teacher asked the class to question the source of the data before recording it in the lab notebook.

s.defn: To doubt or challenge the truth, accuracy, or validity of something by asking for evidence or justification; to critically evaluate claims.
ex: Students should question a claim with credible evidence.
The class questioned the claim before accepting the conclusion in the worksheet.

s.defn: A unit of mass used in customary systems equal to 16 ounces.
ex: A pound weighs about half a kilogram.
There are sixteen ounces in a pound.

s.defn: The basic monetary unit of the United Kingdom used to price goods.
ex: Prices are listed in pounds.
She paid with a pound coin.

s.defn: A public facility where stray animals are kept and cared for until they can be adopted.
ex: The dog pound houses stray dogs.
The county pound takes in adoptable animals.

s.defn: To strike repeatedly with a heavy instrument or body part.
ex: The metalworker pounds hot steel to shape it in the workshop.
The student pounds clay to refine its consistency.

s.defn: To press or beat into shape by repeated blows; to shape by pounding.
ex: The artisan pounds dough until it becomes smooth.
The sheet is pounded flat to form a panel.

s.defn: A pale yellow fat produced by churning cream, used as a spread on bread and in cooking.
ex: A pat of butter melts on toast during a cooking lesson.
The recipe calls for two tablespoons of butter.

s.defn: To apply butter or margarine to bread, toast, or other food by spreading it across the surface as part of food preparation.
ex: She buttered the toast evenly before serving.
In the recipe you should butter the bread before toasting.

s.defn: To flatter or praise someone in order to gain favor or influence.
ex: The student tried to butter up the teacher with compliments.
She tried to butter up her boss before asking for time off.

s.defn: The sixth month of the Gregorian calendar, comprising 30 days.
ex: June marks the transition from spring to summer.
In temperate zones rainfall often peaks in June.

s.defn: A female given name used in English-language contexts.
ex: Census data show June as a common given name in the early 20th century.
In historical records, the given name June appears frequently in the mid-century.

s.defn: Of or pertaining to the calendar month June, the sixth month of the Gregorian calendar.
ex: June data collection occurred during the third quarter.
The June term begins after the spring semester.

s.defn: Relating to the early part of summer in temperate regions, typically June.
ex: June temperatures rose markedly in the study region.
June rainfall patterns were analyzed for seasonal trend.

s.defn: A specific day on the calendar that identifies the time in a month or year.
ex: The due date for the assignment is Friday.
Record the date on the chart to show progress.

s.defn: The edible sweet fruit of the date palm.
ex: Dates are a nutritious fruit enjoyed in snack packs.
Dried dates are common in baking and energy bars.

s.defn: An arranged social appointment with another person, often for romantic reasons.
ex: They scheduled a date to see a movie.
A first date can help build trust and friendship.

s.defn: A time label used to indicate when something happened or was created.
ex: Please write the date at the top of the form.
The system date auto updates each time the file is saved.

s.defn: To determine or record the calendar date of an event, object, or document.
ex: Scientists date the rocks to estimate their age.
We date the calendar entry to track events.

s.defn: To go on a social outing with a romantic partner.
ex: Some teens date during the later grades of school.
Teachers discuss dating etiquette as students mature.

s.defn: A monetary outlay or expenditure incurred in a given period; the total amount spent by an organization, individual, or project.
ex: The department's annual spend on equipment rose by 8 percent.
Budgetary controls monitor discretionary spend to ensure fiscal discipline.

s.defn: To allocate money by paying out funds to obtain goods or services.
ex: The department spent most of its grant on equipment.
Researchers spent funds allocated for data collection.

s.defn: To devote or allocate time to activities or tasks.
ex: Researchers spent two years collecting data.
The committee spent several weeks preparing the report.

s.defn: To expend energy or effort in pursuit of a goal; to use energy or effort.
ex: Participants expended substantial effort to control variables.
The team expended energy during field operations.

s.defn: A male partner in a marriage; the husband of a wife, typically recognized under civil or religious law and social customs as a spouse.
ex: In many cultures the husband is legally recognized as the head of household.
Social surveys often treat the husband as the primary breadwinner.

s.defn: A person who manages resources economically; a steward of assets; a frugal or prudent keeper of resources.
ex: In traditional households a husband acted as a resource manager.
A prudent husband of the estate saved for drought and famine.

s.defn: To manage and use resources sparingly and prudently over time; to conserve and allocate resources for future use.
ex: The department must husband its finite grant funds to maximize research output.
Researchers should husband scarce energy and time during longitudinal experiments.
